questions.question: For a certain classification, the positive mass m, in grams, of an object must be less than 510 grams. Which inequality represents this situation?
questions.explanation: The mass is positive and less than 510, so 0 < m < 510.

questions.question: In the figure shown, line k intersects lines r and s. If w = 160, which additional piece of information is sufficient to prove that lines r and s are parallel?
questions.explanation: Angles w and y are corresponding angles on line k. If y = 160 = w, then r and s are parallel.

questions.question: 6(x − 4) = (x − 4) + 6. If x is the solution to the given equation, what is the value of x − 4?

The equation d = 29w + 100 gives the total amount of money d, in dollars, that James plans to save w weeks after he starts to save. What is the total amount of money, in dollars, he plans to save in 10 weeks?
The function f is defined by f(x) = |x|/a − 14, where a < 0. What is the product of f(15a) and f(8a)?
questions.explanation: Since a < 0, |15a|/a = −15 and |8a|/a = −8. So f(15a) = −29 and f(8a) = −22, and the product is 638.

questions.question:
a(9 − x) = 36 − 4x
In the given equation, a is a constant. The equation has exactly one solution. Which of the following CANNOT be the value of a?
questions.explanation: Rewrite as (4 − a)x = 36 − 9a. If a = 4 this becomes 0 = 0, which has infinitely many solutions; any other a gives exactly one solution.

questions.question:
(x − 2) − 8(y + 3) = 123
(x − 2) + 8(y + 3) = 432
The solution to the given system of equations is (x, y). What is the value of 10(x − 2)?
questions.explanation: Adding the equations gives 2(x − 2) = 555, so x − 2 = 277.5 and 10(x − 2) = 2,775.

questions.question: If (x + 3)<sup>2</sup> = 39, what is the value of x<sup>2</sup> + 6x?
questions.explanation: Expanding, x² + 6x + 9 = 39, so x² + 6x = 30.

questions.question: The function h is defined by h(x) = a^x + b, where a and b are positive constants. The graph of y = h(x) in the xy−plane passes through the points (0, 10) and (2, 13). What is the value of ab?
questions.explanation: h(0) = 1 + b = 10 gives b = 9; h(2) = a^2 + 9 = 13 gives a = 2. So ab = 18.

questions.question:
y = 3x + 13
y = 3x2 + 13
Which ordered pair (x, y) is a solution to the given system of equations?
questions.explanation: Setting 3x + 13 = 3x^2 + 13 gives 3x^2 − 3x = 0, so x = 0 or x = 1. Only x = 0 appears in the choices, and then y = 13, giving (0, 13).

questions.question: x<sup>2</sup> − 100 = 0. How many distinct real solutions does the given equation have?
questions.explanation: x^2 = 100 gives x = 10 or x = −10, which is exactly two solutions.

questions.question: Each of the following frequency tables represents a data set. Which of these frequency tables represents the data set with the smallest standard deviation?
questions.explanation: In A most values are exactly 5 and the rest are only 1 away, so the data are the most tightly clustered around the mean.

questions.question:
The scatterplot shows the relationship between two variables, x and y. A line of best fit is also shown.
Which of the following equations best represents the line of best fit shown?
questions.explanation: The line crosses the y-axis near 3 and rises about 5 for every 3 units right, so y = (5/3)x + 3.

questions.question: A box contains 23 red buttons and 27 blue buttons. If one of these buttons is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting a red button? (Express your answer as a decimal or fraction, not as a percent.)
questions.explanation: Total 50 buttons, 23 red: 23/50 = 0.46.

questions.question: Liam has $150 in an account. Each year he expects to have 2.8% more money in the account than he had the previous year. Which of the following models best describes how Liam expects the money in his account to change over time?
questions.explanation: Growing by the same percent each year multiplies the amount by 1.028 each year, which is increasing exponential growth.

A department store sells pants in three lengths: short, regular, and long. The table above summarizes the distribution of pant length, by color, for all the pants in the store. A pair of pants is selected at random. What is the probability of selecting a pair of pants that is brown, given that the pair of pants is regular length? (Express your answer as a decimal or fraction, not as a percent.)
questions.explanation: Among the 60 regular-length pants, 21 are brown, so the probability is 21/60 = 7/20 = 0.35.

questions.question: A triangle has a base length of 82 centimeters and a height of 164 centimeters. What is the area, in square centimeters, of the triangle?
In triangle QRS, what is the value of tan y°?
questions.explanation: Angle y is at S. The side opposite it is QR = 4 and the adjacent side is RS = 10, so tan y = 4/10.

questions.question: Cube B has a volume of 125 cubic inches. The length of each edge of cube A is k times the length of each edge of cube B. If cube A has a volume of 3,375 cubic inches, what is the value of k?
questions.explanation: Cube B has edge 5 and cube A has edge 15 (15^3 = 3,375), so k = 15/5 = 3.

questions.question: On a plot of land, 52.0% of the square footage is farmland and the remaining square footage is pasture. There are buildings on exactly 21.5% of the square footage of the farmland, and there are buildings on exactly 14.0% of the square footage of the pasture. If there are buildings on exactly p% of the square footage of the plot of land, what is the value of p?
If 4(2x + 11) − 2(2x − 5) = −9 + 13x, what is the value of 12x?
questions.explanation: 4x + 54 = 13x − 9 gives 9x = 63, so x = 7 and 12x = 84.

questions.question: What is the y-intercept of the graph of 3x + 2y = 96 in the xy-plane?
questions.explanation: Set x = 0: 2y = 96, so y = 48.

questions.question: In the figure shown, WZ and XY intersect at point Q, YQ = 36, WQ = 90, WX = 70, and XQ = 150. What is the length of YZ?
questions.explanation: The angles at W and Y are equal and the angles at Q are vertical angles, so triangle WQX is similar to triangle YQZ. YZ/WX = YQ/WQ = 36/90, so YZ = 70(0.4) = 28.

questions.question: A shopper goes to a pet store to buy dog food and treats. The shopper has $20. Each can of food costs $1.87, and each bag of treats costs $2.37. Which inequality represents the relationship between the number of cans of food, c, and the number of bags of treats, t, the shopper can buy?
questions.explanation: Total spending 1.87c + 2.37t can't exceed $20.

questions.explanation: Multiplying the first equation by 3/2 gives 12x + 48y = 45, the second equation, so the two equations describe the same line and have infinitely many intersection points.

The function f is defined by f(x) = 15x5. The graph of y = f(−x) + c in the xy−plane, where c is a positive integer constant, has an x−intercept at (r, 0) and a y−intercept at (0, t), where r and t are constants. Which of the following must be true about r and t?
questions.explanation: The function is y = −15x^5 + c. Then t = c > 0, and setting y = 0 gives x^5 = c/15 > 0, so r > 0.

questions.question:
The functions f and g are defined by the given equations, where x ≥ 0. Which of the following equations displays, as a constant or coefficient, the maximum value of the function it defines, where x ≥ 0?
I. f(x) = 16(1.25)x + 43
II. g(x) = 6(0.75)x
questions.explanation: f grows without bound, so it has no maximum. g decreases from g(0) = 6, so its maximum 6 appears as the coefficient.

questions.question: An exponential function f is defined by f(x) = c<sup>x</sup>, where c is a constant greater than 1. If f(7) = 9 · f(5), what is the value of c?
The scatterplot has 13 data points in an exponential pattern trending up from left to right. Which of the following equations is the most appropriate model for the data shown in the scatterplot?
questions.explanation: The points level off near y = 19 on the left, so the model has a vertical shift of +18. The point (0, 24) gives 6(1)+18 = 24, and (4.3, 57) gives about 6(6.6)+18 ≈ 58.

questions.question: Stefan purchased 500 feet of fencing. He used 80% of this fencing to surround a vegetable garden. How many feet of fencing did Stefan use to surround the vegetable garden?

An exponential model for the number of squirrels in a certain area estimates that there were 200 squirrels in the area in the year 2003, and that at the end of each 4-year period for the next 20 years, the number of squirrels in the area was 120% more than the number at the end of the previous 4-year period. Which of the following equations represents this model, where N is the estimated number of squirrels in this area t years after 2003, and 0 ≤ t ≤ 20?
questions.explanation: 120% more means a factor of 1 + 1.20 = 2.20 every 4 years, so N = 200(2.20)^(t/4).

questions.question: For two acute angles, ∠Q and ∠R, cos(Q) = sin(R). The measures, in degrees, of ∠Q and ∠R are x + 61 and 4x + 4, respectively. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: cos(Q) = sin(R) means the acute angles are complementary: (x + 61) + (4x + 4) = 90, so 5x = 25 and x = 5.

questions.question: A partially filled container containing 26 milliliters of water is placed under a leaky faucet that produces one 0.08-milliliter drop of water every 8 seconds. Until the container is full, which of the following can be used to represent the volume v, in milliliters, of water in the container t seconds after it is placed under the faucet, where t is a multiple of 8?
questions.explanation: The rate is 0.08/8 = 0.01 milliliters per second, starting from 26.

questions.question:
34x + 83y = 370
The given equation represents the volume of mulch x, in cubic feet, and the volume of soil y, in cubic feet, in a mixture of mulch and soil that weighs 370 pounds. If the volume of soil in the mixture is 2 cubic feet, what is the volume of mulch in the mixture, in cubic feet?
questions.explanation: Substituting y = 2 gives 34x + 166 = 370, so 34x = 204 and x = 6.
